concepts.title: Polynomial rings & monomial orders
concepts.blurb: A monomial order on $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is a total well-ordering of monomials respecting multiplication. The three workhorses — lex, grlex, grevlex — pick out different leading terms of the same polynomial; changing the order changes the leading term.

concepts.title: The multivariable division algorithm
concepts.blurb: Given a monomial order and an ordered tuple $(g_1,\dots,g_s)$, division writes $f = \sum a_i g_i + r$ where no monomial of $r$ is divisible by $\mathrm{LT}(g_i)$. Unlike single-variable division, $r$ depends on the divisor order — the defect Gröbner bases fix.

concepts.title: Gröbner bases: definition
concepts.blurb: A finite $G\subset I$ is a Gröbner basis when $\langle\mathrm{LT}(g_i)\rangle = \langle\mathrm{LT}(I)\rangle$. Then division by $G$ has a unique remainder and ideal membership becomes a single algorithm. Hilbert's basis theorem guarantees existence in $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$.

concepts.title: S-polynomials & Buchberger's criterion
concepts.blurb: The S-polynomial $S(f,g) = (\gamma/\mathrm{LT}(f))f - (\gamma/\mathrm{LT}(g))g$, $\gamma=\mathrm{lcm}(\mathrm{LM}(f),\mathrm{LM}(g))$, is a syzygy that cancels leading terms. Buchberger: $G$ is a Gröbner basis iff every $S(g_i,g_j)$ reduces to zero modulo $G$.

concepts.title: Buchberger's algorithm
concepts.blurb: Repeatedly compute S-polynomials of pairs, reduce modulo the current basis, and append nonzero remainders until every S-polynomial reduces to zero. Termination by the ACC on $\langle\mathrm{LT}(F)\rangle$. Worst case is doubly exponential (Mayr–Meyer).

concepts.title: Reduced Gröbner bases
concepts.blurb: $G$ is reduced when each element is monic and no monomial of any $g$ is divisible by $\mathrm{LT}(g')$ for $g'\ne g$. For a fixed monomial order, every nonzero ideal has a *unique* reduced Gröbner basis — the canonical computational representative.

concepts.title: Elimination ideals
concepts.blurb: Under lex with $x_1>\cdots>x_n$, the Elimination Theorem says $G\cap k[x_{i+1},\dots,x_n]$ is a Gröbner basis of $I\cap k[x_{i+1},\dots,x_n]$. Computes implicit equations of parametrized varieties and intersections of ideals via $tI+(1-t)J$.

concepts.title: Solving polynomial systems & implicitization
concepts.blurb: Zero-dimensional ideals have a triangular lex Gröbner basis that solves systems by back-substitution; parametric varieties yield implicit equations by eliminating parameters. The capstone of computational commutative algebra: ideal → algorithm → numerical or geometric answer.
